title: Safe encounter-to-order join
scenario: Join encounter and order tables without inflating encounter counts.
task: Use pre-aggregation or count distinct encounter IDs. Explain why raw row counts differ.
solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS joined_rows, COUNT(DISTINCT e.encounter_id) AS encounters FROM encounters e LEFT JOIN medication_orders o ON o.encounter_id=e.encounter_id;
expected: Joined rows exceed encounter count when encounters have multiple orders; distinct encounters remain 300.

title: Window ranking
scenario: Rank departments by mean length of stay, retaining ties.
task: Use DENSE_RANK over department-level means.
solution: WITH d AS (SELECT department, AVG(length_of_stay_days) mean_los FROM encounters GROUP BY department) SELECT department, ROUND(mean_los,2), DENSE_RANK() OVER(ORDER BY mean_los DESC) AS rnk FROM d ORDER BY rnk,department;
expected: Five departments ranked; tied means share rank.

title: 30-day readmission proxy
scenario: Calculate supplied readmission-flag rate by department.
task: Denominator is eligible index encounters; do not infer causal quality.
solution: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(readmission_30d_flag) AS flagged, ROUND(100.0*SUM(readmission_30d_flag)/COUNT(*),2) AS pct FROM encounters GROUP BY department;
expected: Rates vary by department; all records are synthetic.

title: Latest record per patient
scenario: Select the most recent encounter per patient.
task: Use ROW_NUMBER partitioned by patient and deterministic tie-break.
solution: WITH x AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY admission_date DESC, encounter_id DESC) rn FROM encounters) SELECT * FROM x WHERE rn=1;
expected: At most one row per patient.

title: Anti-join orphan audit
scenario: Find medication orders with no encounter.
task: Use NOT EXISTS; compare with LEFT JOIN IS NULL.
solution: SELECT o.* FROM medication_orders o WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM encounters e WHERE e.encounter_id=o.encounter_id);
expected: 41 intentional orphan order rows in this training dataset.

title: NULL-safe cost analysis
scenario: Calculate order value without treating missing unit cost as zero.
task: Report missing-cost count separately; sum only known values.
solution: SELECT COUNT(*) total_rows, SUM(CASE WHEN unit_cost_inr IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) missing_cost_rows, SUM(quantity*unit_cost_inr) known_value_inr FROM medication_orders;
expected: Missing costs remain unknown; aggregate is partial known value.

title: Rolling 7-day volume
scenario: Create a daily order count and seven-calendar-day rolling total.
task: Aggregate to date first; use ROWS frame and note missing dates limitation.
solution: WITH daily AS (SELECT order_date, COUNT(*) n FROM medication_orders GROUP BY order_date) SELECT order_date,n,SUM(n) OVER(ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) rolling_7_rows FROM daily;
expected: Seven rows, not necessarily seven calendar days if dates are absent.

title: Cohort entry and follow-up
scenario: Define index encounter and subsequent encounter within 30 days.
task: State date boundaries and patient-level grain.
solution: WITH x AS (SELECT patient_id, admission_date, encounter_id, LEAD(admission_date) OVER(PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY admission_date) next_date FROM encounters) SELECT *, CASE WHEN julianday(next_date)-julianday(admission_date) BETWEEN 1 AND 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END subsequent_30d FROM x;
expected: A subsequent encounter is not automatically an unplanned readmission.

title: Deduplicate business records
scenario: Identify duplicate-like order rows without deleting automatically.
task: Use business key candidates and ROW_NUMBER; preserve audit trail.
solution: SELECT encounter_id,therapeutic_class,order_date,COUNT(*) candidate_rows FROM medication_orders GROUP BY encounter_id,therapeutic_class,order_date HAVING COUNT(*)>1;
expected: Candidates require review; repeated same-class orders can be legitimate.

title: Conditional aggregation
scenario: Produce order count and known cost by department.
task: Join department at encounter grain after order aggregation.
solution: WITH o AS (SELECT encounter_id,COUNT(*) order_lines,SUM(quantity*unit_cost_inr) known_cost FROM medication_orders GROUP BY encounter_id) SELECT e.department,SUM(COALESCE(o.order_lines,0)) lines,SUM(o.known_cost) known_cost FROM encounters e LEFT JOIN o ON o.encounter_id=e.encounter_id GROUP BY e.department;
expected: No fan-out; missing unit costs remain excluded from known cost.

title: Percentile and median portability
scenario: Compute median LOS with portable strategy.
task: Explain SQLite lacks built-in percentile_cont in common builds; provide sorted extraction or extension-specific syntax.
solution: SELECT department,length_of_stay_days FROM encounters WHERE length_of_stay_days IS NOT NULL ORDER BY department,length_of_stay_days;
expected: Calculate median per department in client/Python or PostgreSQL percentile_cont.

title: Query plan and indexing
scenario: Inspect a date-filter query and justify an index.
task: Use EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN in SQLite; avoid index proliferation.
solution: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT * FROM medication_orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-03-31';
expected: Compare plan before/after a suitable index; document measured context.

title: Cohort denominator integrity
scenario: Compare patient count, encounter count and order count.
task: Never mix grains in one denominator.
solution: SELECT 'encounters' entity,COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) distinct_people,COUNT(*) rows FROM encounters UNION ALL SELECT 'orders',COUNT(DISTINCT encounter_id),COUNT(*) FROM medication_orders;
expected: Different grains should produce different counts; order encounter count includes orphan keys.

title: Pivot-style aggregation
scenario: Create department-by-drug-class summary.
task: Use conditional aggregation; include unknown class bucket.
solution: SELECT department,SUM(CASE WHEN therapeutic_class='Antihypertensive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) antihypertensive_lines,SUM(CASE WHEN therapeutic_class IS NULL OR therapeutic_class='' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) unknown_class_lines FROM medication_orders o LEFT JOIN encounters e ON e.encounter_id=o.encounter_id GROUP BY department;
expected: Orphan orders may have NULL department; retain or report separately.

title: Date boundary correctness
scenario: Filter all orders in a month safely.
task: Prefer half-open interval over timestamp end-of-day literals.
solution: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM medication_orders WHERE order_date >= '2026-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-02-01';
expected: Includes all January timestamps if column stores ISO date/time.

title: CTE cohort with exclusion
scenario: Build a CKD cohort excluding missing baseline SBP.
task: Define missingness and exclusion count explicitly.
solution: SELECT COUNT(*) eligible FROM encounters WHERE ckd_flag=1 AND baseline_sbp IS NOT NULL;
expected: Report CKD records excluded for missing SBP separately.

title: Medication utilisation intensity
scenario: Calculate order lines per encounter by department.
task: Use encounter denominator and state that order lines are not administrations.
solution: WITH o AS (SELECT encounter_id,COUNT(*) n FROM medication_orders GROUP BY encounter_id) SELECT e.department,COUNT(*) encounters, SUM(COALESCE(o.n,0)) lines,ROUND(1.0*SUM(COALESCE(o.n,0))/COUNT(*),2) lines_per_encounter FROM encounters e LEFT JOIN o ON o.encounter_id=e.encounter_id GROUP BY e.department;
expected: Metric measures order-line intensity only.

title: Incremental load watermark
scenario: Select records changed after a stored watermark.
task: Discuss late-arriving records, inclusive/exclusive boundary and idempotent merge.
solution: SELECT * FROM medication_orders WHERE updated_at > '2026-03-01T00:00:00';
expected: Production pipeline also needs overlap/reconciliation or CDC guarantees.

title: Case-mix stratification
scenario: Compare LOS within age bands and diabetes status.
task: Stratification is descriptive; small cells require suppression.
solution: SELECT CASE WHEN age<40 THEN '<40' WHEN age<65 THEN '40-64' ELSE '65+' END age_band,diabetes_flag,COUNT(*) n,AVG(length_of_stay_days) mean_los FROM encounters GROUP BY age_band,diabetes_flag;
expected: Interpret cell sizes and confounding.

title: Data quality exception rate
scenario: Calculate missing SBP and impossible LOS checks.
task: Return numerator and denominator, not just percentages.
solution: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN baseline_sbp IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) missing_sbp, SUM(CASE WHEN length_of_stay_days<0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) negative_los,COUNT(*) denominator FROM encounters;
expected: Explicitly state validation rules and exceptions.
